oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Protecting Digital Footprints: A Selective Web History Sanitization Tool for Domestic Violence Survivors
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study introduces a novel solution that is designed to protect the privacy of domestic violence survivors when seeking online support. It enables survivors to access essential online resources without leaving digital footprints that may lead to further abuse by their violent partners. The study employs the principles of the design science framework to develop and evaluate a system for selective web history sanitization. The implemented system effectively deletes traces related to support websites while preserving unrelated browsing history to avoid the abuser’s suspicion, ensuring both usability and privacy. This work contributes a novel artifact that addresses a critical societal challenge, providing domestic violence survivors with a secure, adaptive, and privacy-preserving tool to seek online supports with confidence. It offers a significant step forward in protecting and empowering vulnerable populations, particularly those with limited technical expertise in the digital age. Additionally, this work offers practical insights for organizations that support survivors by advocating for the development and use of privacy-focused tools and practices to make their digital services more effective and safer.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: AI-Based Load Balancing Using Decision Tree Regressor for Parallel Matrix Computation in Cloud Environments
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cloud computing is an evolving technology of current information systems that supports dynamic sharing and elastic provision of resources and services. With increasing demands for computational resources, efficient workload assignment has become an important challenge. Current load balancing methods based on traditional approaches fail to suit dynamic server performance and contribute to the inefficient utilization of available resources, latency, and delays. In response to this challenge, this paper suggests an AI-driven load balancer based on a decision tree regressor to dynamically control task allocation within a parallel cloud system. The system operates to handle computationally heavy tasks, i.e., matrix multiplication, across different servers based on real-time performance measures such as Central Processing Unit (CPU) usage, memory utilization, time of execution, and networking latency. Model training was done with historical data obtained from past executions, incorporated into the web server to facilitate adaptive decision-making. It was tested experimentally with different levels of server scalability as well as matrix complexity. It was contrasted with a static, manual load balancer. All critical performance measures were found to be significantly improved by the AI-based methodology, with the total execution time reduced from 7,060 milliseconds to 1,000 milliseconds; network latency was also reduced to 5.12 ms, down from 214 ms; and the method reduced the overall use of CPU by 33% and overall use of memory by more than 85%. These findings confirm that intelligent, data-driven load balancing offers superior scalability, responsiveness, and efficiency for cloud-based parallel processing systems.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Multilingual Hybrid News Recommendation Framework for Educational Web Portals
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: University web portals increasingly serve as vital platforms for academic information sharing, yet effective news recommendation in resource-constrained, multilingual environments remains challenging due to limited labeled data, sparse user profiles, and linguistic diversity. This study presents a modular hybrid news recommendation framework tailored for educational web portals in low-resource settings. The approach integrates lexical methods, specifically Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF–IDF) and Best Match 25 (BM25), with semantic retrieval based on Sentence-BERT (SBERT), combined with unsupervised clustering for topical diversification and a fuzzy-logic fusion layer to integrate heterogeneous similarity signals. A publicly available multilingual dataset of 1,389 university news articles was collected via a custom crawler, and a Flask-based API was implemented for real-time recommendation. Evaluation relies on an automatic hybrid ground truth generated by fusing SBERT, TF–IDF, and BM25 signals. On the ground truth subset, the hybrid model attains Precision@5 = 0.96 and NDCG@5 = 0.945, outperforming SBERT (Precision@5 = 0.93; NDCG@5 = 0.859), with improvements shown to be statistically significant (paired t-test on NDCG@5, p < 1e-5). Clustering enhances thematic diversity (entropy 1.697 vs. 0.032), reducing concentration on repeated announcements. Multilingual experiments demonstrate consistently high precision across Arabic, Kurdish, and English but reveal substantially lower recall for underrepresented languages, highlighting dataset imbalance and representation challenges. Fusion weights were tuned on a validation split to balance precision and recall while mitigating the dominance of any single signal across languages and content types. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and extensible solution for multilingual academic news recommendation in scenarios where interaction data are scarce, offering a practical foundation for future work on language-aware preprocessing, human validation of labels, and supervised re-ranking.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Suitability of Sprouted and Fresh Three Potato Cultivars for Chip Manufacture: A Chemical and Sensory Evaluation
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Potatoes are a globally important crop and a key raw material for the production of chips. Sprouting during potato storage is a critical problem that alters chemical and sensory attributes such as sugar accumulation, starch reduction, and firmness loss, which negatively affect chip quality. However, limited studies have addressed these changes across cultivars under local conditions. The present study explored the influence of fresh potato (at harvest) and sprouting stages (non-sprouted, and sprouted at 1 cm and 2 cm length) on the chemical properties and sensory quality of three potato chip cultivars (Crozo, Hermes, and Lady Rosetta), which are widely grown in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. To ensure clarity of the experimental design, the study specifically evaluated these three cultivars across four developmental stages to assess their chemical and sensory quality for chip production. After that, the results indicated that Crozo exhibited the highest dry matter (29.78%) and starch (22.53%) at 2 cm sprouting, indicating strong frying potential. Lady Rosetta exhibited the least weight loss (5.85%) and the highest firmness (33.02 N) at harvest. TSS increased after storage, peaking in Lady Rosetta (8.67 %), while total sugar content decreased during sprouting to 0.089%. Sensory scores for chips declined with increased sprout length. Crozo and Lady Rosetta maintained a better appearance, flavor, and texture during the sprouting stages than Hermes. Overall, the cultivar and sprouting stages had a significant influence on quality. Fresh and non-sprouted potatoes are recommended for optimal chip quality. The results concluded that Crozo and Lady Rosetta cultivars are most suitable for storage conditions and processing due to their favorable chemical traits and sensory performance.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Finite Element Study on the Structural Behavior of a Dual-Axis Solar Tracking System
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Solar panels have become a highly effective and widely adopted source of renewable energy. Extensive research has been devoted to improving the materials used in photovoltaic systems to enhance efficiency, durability, and performance. Continuous efforts have also focused on strategies to maximize solar energy capture; from materials used to determining the optimal angle and direction for panel installation for optimal energy capture. Within this context, this study presents the design and structural analysis of an innovative dual-axis solar tracker, developed and simulated using SolidWorks. The design consists of three main components: the main structure, which can hold up to a total of 18 panels arranged in a 3x6 matrix; the rotating structure, to which the main structure is attached via two flanged bearings at the ends to provide tilt motion; and the stationary base, to which the rotating structure is connected via a slew bearing that enables rotation in the east-west direction. The overall design accounts for a total system weight of approximately 4000 kg. To ensure safe operation, Finite Element Analysis is conducted under extreme-case wind loading conditions to assess structural integrity. Key results included a maximum von Mises stress of 196.6 MPa, a maximum deflection of 37.81 mm, and a minimum factor of safety of 1.122. Convergence is successfully achieved for all components, with relative errors below 1%, confirming the reliability and accuracy of the simulation outcomes.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Effectiveness of Psychoeducation to Reduce Relapse Among Substance Users: An Interventional Study
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Relapse rates among substance users are generally higher in the early stages following substance use cessation. Nevertheless, correctional facilities are seeking effective strategies to reduce the risk of relapse among incarcerated substance users. This study developed and assessed a psychoeducational program to reduce the risk of relapse among substance users using a quasi-experimental design. We recruited 102 incarcerated substance users from a correctional facility and divided them into two equal groups. The pretest, program implementation, and posttest were conducted from July 1, 2024, to March 2, 2025, using the Stimulant Relapse Risk Scale-35. Paired t-tests and a linear regression analysis were used to evaluate program effectiveness and identify the predictive factors for reducing the risks of relapse, respectively. The sample was predominantly male (82.2%). Approximately 51.2% and 56.4% participants in the control and experimental groups, respectively, were using methamphetamines. Participants in the experimental group showed a significant improvement following program implementation (p < 0.001). Significant predictors of greater improvement following the program’s implementation were good financial status, being divorced, living with a spouse, living alone, and using opium. Conversely, significant predictors of lower improvement included having a bachelor’s degree, having parents with substance use disorders, smoking fewer than 10 cigarettes per day, starting to smoke at an older age, and using alcohol. Our findings underscore the necessity of psychoeducational programs in correctional facilities to help substance users participate in programs, thereby reducing their risk of relapse.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Differentially Private Reward Functions in Markov Decision Processes: Policy Synthesis and Tradeoffs
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Policy synthesis in Markov decision processes uses a known reward function to compute a policy that maximizes it. However, onlookers may infer reward functions by observing agents, which can reveal sensitive information. Therefore, in this paper we introduce and compare two methods for privatizing reward functions in policy synthesis for multi-agent Markov decision processes, which generalize Markov decision processes. Reward functions are privatized using differential privacy, a statistical framework for protecting sensitive data. The methods we develop perturb (i) each agent's individual reward function or (ii) the joint reward function shared by all agents. We prove that both of these methods are differentially private and show approach (i) provides better performance. We then develop guidelines for selecting reward functions to achieve high performance while remaining private, and we quantify the increase in computation required to compute policies with privatized rewards. Numerical simulations are performed on several examples, and these examples show that even relatively strong differential privacy (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\epsilon =1.3$</tex-math></inline-formula>) induces as little as a 5% decrease in performance and 0.016% increase in computation time.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A High-Power Frequency Doubler-Based Terahertz Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave Transceiver Front-End
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This paper presents a high-performance terahertz frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) transceiver front-end operating at 139.5–148.5 GHz, which leverages a high-power frequency doubler to address critical challenges in terahertz amplification. A novel modular architecture is introduced to circumvent the limitations of power amplifiers (PAs), enabling a breakthrough in power handling capability. In the transmitter, a GaN Schottky diode-based doubler integrated with meta-atom resonant microstructures achieves an output power exceeding 17 dBm by enhancing electric field coupling and power conversion efficiency. The receiver employs a custom subharmonic mixer combined with a low-noise amplifier (LNA) placed adjacent to the feed source, effectively reducing the noise figure. A compact waveguide-to-microstrip transition and cavity filter assembly in the system packaging suppresses spurious emissions below −43.84 dBc. Experimental results demonstrate an input P1dB of −22.5 dBm (surpassing the −24 dBm specification), with a switchable IF bandwidth (50/90 MHz modes) for adaptive ranging. The total gain reaches 85.36 dB, and the manual gain control (MGC) accuracy achieves 0.515 dB RMS. The front-end balances power efficiency, spectral purity (phase noise ≤−92.5 dBc/Hz at 1 kHz), and linearity, providing a reliable hardware platform for high-resolution radar imaging, non-destructive testing, and real-time sensing applications.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: CLAPC: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Architecture for Automated Passenger Counting From Video Streams in Public Transport
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Information on passenger occupancy in public transport is crucial for service providers to enable accurate revenue sharing within transportation networks. This requires reliable methods to count boarding and alighting passengers and to differentiate between passenger categories, such as those requiring a valid ticket. In previous work, a recurrent Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network (NAPC) was applied to depth videos captured by time-of-flight sensors mounted above train doors to perform passenger counting and height-based differentiation. In this work, we investigate whether this approach can be transferred to 2D gray-scale video data recorded from the same overhead perspective, where explicit depth information is unavailable. To this end, we extend the LSTM architecture by integrating a convolutional neural network, resulting in the CLAPC model, which improves the extraction of image features. Additionally, region-of-interest cropping and spatial down-sampling are explored to better address privacy concerns, and the training procedure is refined to reduce undercounting. Applying CLAPC to depth data improves counting accuracy compared to NAPC. Moreover, high accuracies are achieved on 2D video data despite the absence of explicit depth information. The highest performance is obtained using down-sampled door-path crops, yielding mean accuracies of 99.73% for boarding and 99.87% for alighting passengers. On depth data, accuracies of 99.79% and 99.97% are achieved for boarding and alighting, respectively. These results meet the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\pm ~1\%$ </tex-math></inline-formula> accuracy requirement of VDV Guideline 457. The 95% confidence intervals from an equivalence test lie within the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\pm ~1\%$ </tex-math></inline-formula> bounds, which confirms that CLAPC is statistically robust.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Semi-Supervised Framework for Road Condition Assessment: From Minor Surface Distress to Post-Disaster Failures
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Accurate road-condition segmentation is crucial for intelligent transportation systems (ITS), enabling autonomous driving and post-disaster recovery. Yet, most prior studies focus on binary or low-class segmentation, limiting applicability to complex scenes where subtle surface degradations and large-scale obstructions coexist. To address this gap, we present a unified framework for pixel-level segmentation across 11 road-condition classes using a hybrid dataset integrating the Post-Disaster Road Dataset Japan (PDRDD-J), the Social Media Image Dataset for Disaster Road Damage Object Detection (SoDR), and the Road Damage Dataset 2022 (RDD2022-J). The defined classes include background, road, manhole cover, alligator crack, linear crack, pothole, vehicle, natural blockage, structural blockage, sinkhole, and collapsed road. To learn this label space under limited supervision, we propose F-UNet, a Feature-Level Data Extractor (FLDE)-guided extension of U-Net integrated into a standard teacher–student self-training protocol and trained through progressive pairwise specialization. Unlike conventional U-Net variants that rely solely on global multi-class training, F-UNet derives FLDE guidance through pairwise road–damage patch training and injects it during decoding to better handle class imbalance and thin, low-contrast defects. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent gains over strong baselines, supported by high-confidence class-wise analysis, confusion-matrix analysis, and error and uncertainty-based failure-mode characterization under disaster edge cases. On a held-out test set, the teacher model achieves 0.8652 mIoU, representing a 15.5% improvement over standard U-Net and outperforming U-Net<monospace>++</monospace>, DeepLabV3<monospace>+</monospace>, SegNet, and FCN under the same supervision setting. In the semi-supervised configuration, the student model further improves to 0.8727 mIoU. The F-UNet source code is available at <uri>https://github.com/EdaTsujimoto/F-UNET</uri>

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Reputation-Based Hyperledger Fabric for Private and Scalable Data Sharing in CAVs
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The operation of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) is primarily driven by the continuous exchange of data from various sources, including in-vehicle sensors, neighbouring vehicles, and roadside infrastructure.This continuous data exchange results in the accumulation of large volumes of data with dimensionality, which is essential for accurate decision-making in autonomous driving functions. Shared data often encompasses highly sensitive data such as precise vehicular location, driver identification and behavioural patterns.As a result, there is an increasing public concern over the privacy implications associated with the extensive data exchanges. In this context, this research investigates access control mechanisms that ensure privacy and trust in CAVs. We propose a Reputation-based Hyperledger Fabric (RepHLF) framework, a novel privacy-preserving architecture that integrates across-channel Hyperledger Fabric blockchain with a dynamic, multi-metric reputation model for CAV environments. The reputation mechanism evaluates vehicles based on three parameters: behavioural integrity, legitimacy, and historical communication reliability. Each parameter evolves using exponential decay functions to reflect temporal relevance. Data access is subsequently restricted to trusted vehicles only, according to their computed reputation index. The performance of RepHLF is evaluated in terms of accuracy, latency, memory usage, privacy loss, and communication overhead using Hyperledger Caliper. Simulation results demonstrate ultra-low average latency of approximately 201 ms, minimal communication cost of 2.8 KB per transaction, Throughput of 4.99 TPS and high learning accuracy of 99.94%, while maintaining a bounded privacy loss of 3.12%. The integrated reputation mechanism within the consensus algorithm further enhances network reliability by dynamically identifying untrusted vehicles and restricting their transaction requests. Further analysis of the proposed model, RepHLF, against existing reputation-based models demonstrates superior dynamic trust evolution and robust privacy preservation.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Multi-Mode Hybrid Control Strategy With Seamless Transition for Constant-Current Charging in LCC Resonant Capacitor Charging Power Supply
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: A multi-mode hybrid control strategy with seamless switching capability is proposed to address the issues of excessively wide operating frequency range and low light-load efficiency in traditional LCC resonant capacitor charging power supplies(CCPS) under constant-current charging control. The strategy achieves smooth transition of charging voltage by switching topologies in stages: half-bridge mode is adopted in the initial charging phase, PWM-PFM hybrid mode in the middle phase, and full-bridge mode in the later phase. A steady-state model of the LCC resonant converter under PWM-PFM hybrid control is established based on the fundamental harmonic approximation (FHA), and the DC voltage gain expression is derived. A seamless mode-switching mechanism is designed, effectively suppressing current surges during transitions. A 650 V/1 A constant-current charging experimental platform was built for validation. Experimental results show that, compared to conventional constant-current charging control, the proposed strategy reduces the converter's operating frequency range by approximately 56.8%, improves the overall average efficiency by 7.3%, achieves a maximum efficiency increase of 15.7%, and eliminates current surge during mode transitions.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Source-Level EMI Suppression Scheme for Inverters Based on Staircased Voltage Shaping of Series-Connected IGBTs
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Inverters generate significant EMI due to their rapid switching operations. This paper proposes an EMI suppression scheme at the source level based on a series IGBT topology and voltage shaping. By reshaping the output voltage waveform, the scheme periodically suppresses the EMI source. Furthermore, staircase voltage shaping is implemented using a CPLD-based sequential gate drive circuit, eliminating the need for complex modifications to existing gate drive circuits. Experimental results on an 1140 V explosion-proof induction motor drive platform demonstrate that this method achieves harmonic attenuation of 4–20 dBμV within a 2 MHz bandwidth period. Compared to traditional two-level inverters, total switching losses are reduced by around 70%. Periodic EMI suppression also simplifies the design complexity of other EMI mitigation methods within the system. Its periodic nature also enhances design predictability. Moreover, this approach leverages the flexibility and scalability of the series IGBT structure to provide a practical solution for high-voltage inverter systems. It enables source-level EMI suppression without significantly increasing system complexity or cost.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Direct Adaptive Control of Photovoltaic Boost Converters With Ultra-Low Input Capacitance
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Boost converters are widely used in the voltage step-up stage of photovoltaic (PV) inverters due to their simple construction. These converters must operate in both maximum power point tracking and limited power tracking modes, which requires effective regulation of both PV voltage and inductor current using a dual-loop control structure. Reducing the input capacitance to eliminate electrolytic capacitors and increase lifetime, however, introduces significant parametric variations, making the control design challenging and limiting the dynamic performance of the voltage controller. This work proposes a dual-loop adaptive control strategy, comprising an outer voltage loop with model reference adaptive control and an inner current loop with a fixed-gain PI controller. The proposed method resolves issues observed in previous works in both steady-state and transient operation, enabling fast PV voltage tracking with an ultra-low 2 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathrm{\mu }$</tex-math></inline-formula>F input capacitor. Experimental results demonstrate stable operation in both continuous conduction mode and discontinuous conduction mode modes, with a settling time of 7 ms at a switching frequency of 40 kHz, improved dynamic response, and applicability in PV systems under rapidly changing irradiance conditions.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Anatomy-Guided Radiology Report Generation With Pathology-Aware Regional Prompts
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: <italic>Goal:</italic> Radiology report generation holds significant potential to alleviate clinical workloads and streamline medical care. However, achieving high clinical accuracy remains challenging, as radiographs often feature intricate structures and subtle pathologies. <italic>Methods:</italic> To address these challenges, this work introduces an innovative approach that explicitly integrates anatomical and pathological information into report decoding by leveraging pathology-aware regional prompts. Specifically, we develop an anatomical region detector that extracts structured visual features from distinct anatomical areas, coupled with a novel multi-label pathology detector that identifies global abnormalities. <italic>Results:</italic> Our model demonstrates superior report generation performance in natural language generation and clinical efficacy, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods. It achieved scores of 0.394 in BLEU-1, 0.302 in ROUGE-L, and 0.470 in F1, reflecting substantial improvements in both linguistic fluency and medical accuracy. Formal expert evaluations further affirmed the model's potential to elevate radiology practice. <italic>Conclusion:</italic> By integrating anatomical and pathological insights to emulate radiologists' workflow, our model achieves superior accuracy and clinical coherence of radiology reporting. It offers remarkable promise to support clinical decision-making and transform patient management.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Real-Time Safe Production Scheduling via Causal Inference and Hybrid-Event Control
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article proposes a real-time and certifiably safe scheduling framework for cyber-physical manufacturing systems, designed to operate under hybrid discrete–continuous dynamics and deployment-level latency constraints. The approach integrates two core components. First, a <italic>wavelet-invariant causal modeling module</italic> that uncovers multiscale dependencies in sensor data while preserving conditional-independence structure under orthonormal wavelet projections, and second, a <italic>hybrid-event barrier certificate (HRCBC) filter</italic> that enforces hard safety constraints across both continuous flows and discrete event triggers, such as tool changeovers and emergency halts. Departing from traditional methods that assume smooth dynamics or fixed planning horizons, the architecture fuses offline causal discovery with fast, online, safety-filtered control. Causal graphs are learned via orthonormal wavelet projections and refreshed per shift or upon concept-drift detection. Real-time safety is maintained by solving a convex quadratic program with warm starts and p99 latency under 10 ms. The method is validated on two industrial lines (Site-A: EV-module assembly; Site-B: appliance assembly) and on public synthetic benchmarks (SynTwin-Bench), with ablations and multisite simulations. Across the reported testbeds, wavelet-invariant structural transformation+HRCBC improves cycle time by up to 28% and operating cost by 20% relative to the incumbent dispatcher; throughout the reported evaluation horizon, no safety violations were recorded by the independent programmable logic controller (PLC) safety layer, while maintaining PLC-compatible latency. The system is deployable on standard industrial gateways and interoperable with the manufacturing execution system (MES) and PLC via RESTful and open platform communications unified architecture (OPC UA) adapters.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: TPR-S: Two-Phase Routing with Source-Dependent Traffic Distribution Ratios
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Two-phase routing (TPR) is a routing strategy based on segment routing that aims to balance traffic load in two phases. In TPR, a source node distributes traffic to intermediate nodes in the first phase, and each intermediate node forwards it to a destination node in the second phase. Previous studies addressed two models of TPR: TPR-C and TPR-SD. TPR-C distributes traffic to intermediate nodes with a common set of distribution ratios regardless of each source and destination node pair. TPR-SD distributes traffic to intermediate nodes with distribution ratios depending on each source and destination node pair. TPR-SD reduces the network congestion ratio compared to TPR-C, but TPR-SD requires higher deployment complexity. This paper proposes a TPR-based model that enables distribution ratios dependent on each source node but independent of different destination nodes, called TPR-S, to minimize the network congestion ratio under a given traffic matrix. Since TPR-S does not require destination information, it is easier to deploy in an IP network than TPR-SD. In addition, to make TPR-S more easily deployed, we introduce a variant of TPR-S, called even-split TPR-S (TPR-S-ES), where a source node can only evenly distribute traffic to intermediate nodes in the same distribution ratios. We formulate the problems to determine distribution ratios in TPR-S and TPR-S-ES as a linear programming (LP) problem and a mixed-integer LP (MILP) problem, respectively. We introduce a heuristic algorithm for TPR-S-ES to accelerate the computation. Numerical results show that TPR-S reduces network congestion by up to 53.4% compared to shortest path routing and achieves a comparable network congestion with other baseline models. Additionally, TPR-S-ES demonstrates improved performance, particularly in networks with a higher average node degree.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Quantitative Analysis of the Impact of Region of Interest Information on Deep Learning Algorithms for Thyroid Ultrasound Imaging
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: <italic>Goal:</italic> To quantitatively assess the impact of incorporating radiologist-defined Region of Interest (ROI) information in training deep learning models for thyroid ultrasound image classification and lesion localization. Methods: We compared a conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) trained without ROI information, interpreted through Grad-CAM for attention visualization, to Faster R-CNN and YOLOv2 models trained with radiologist-validated ROI masks. We also introduced an adapted mosaic-based composite input, derived from mosaic augmentation but implemented as fixed 1 × 2 and 2 × 2 layouts, to improve class balance and spatial diversity in training. Results: Models trained with ROI guidance achieved higher performance in both localization and classification compared to those trained without ROI. The average classification accuracy increased from about 80% in the baseline CNN to around 85% in ROI-guided models that shows an improvement of approximately 5 percentage points. The mean intersection over union between detected and radiologist-defined ROIs increased from approximately 33% to over 70%. The adapted mosaic input further stabilized performance across epochs and improved sensitivity while maintaining comparable specificity. Conclusions: Incorporating radiologist-defined ROI information and structured mosaic inputs significantly improves both diagnostic accuracy and localization precision. These results demonstrate that integrating ROI-guided learning with context-preserving composite inputs provides a reproducible framework for developing reliable AI systems in thyroid ultrasonography.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Transfer Learning Approach for Generalizing Reinforcement Learning in Autonomous Robot Navigation Using LiDAR: Cross-Platform Adaptation and Obstacle Avoidance
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cross-robot deployment of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) navigation remains difficult in dynamic environments because robot platforms often differ in embodiment, motion constraints, and LiDAR sensing geometry. This article proposes a transfer-learning (TL) framework for LiDAR-based autonomous navigation that reduces source–target observation mismatch through sensor-space alignment and stabilizes target adaptation through policy-preserving fine-tuning. To improve safety in dynamic environments, a lightweight cellular automata (CA)-based predictor is incorporated into the reinforcement-learning objective as a short-horizon, risk-aware shaping term. The proposed framework is validated through a multi-stage experimental protocol. First, a source policy is pretrained in a custom dynamic environment. Second, cross-platform transfer is evaluated in DynaBARN on three heterogeneous target robots: a quadruped, an omniwheel robot, and a differential-drive robot. Third, an additional benchmark across Easy, Medium, and Hard DynaBARN settings compares the proposed method against PPO+TL, DQN+TL, DWA, and TEB with statistical validation. Across the three target robots in DynaBARN, the proposed method achieves success rates of 81.0%–83.1%, collision rates of 5.4%–7.2%, and time-to-goal values of 35.6–39.7 s, yielding the best mean performance among the compared transfer-based baselines. In the difficulty-level benchmark, one-way ANOVA indicates significant group-level differences across metrics, and the proposed method degrades more gracefully than the compared methods while maintaining the best mean results. On a physical quadruped robot, the transferred policy achieves 90.0% success with 10.0% collision under controlled but non-identical obstacle interactions and real sensing/actuation uncertainty. These results indicate that combining sensor-space alignment, policy preservation, and short-horizon motion-risk shaping improves the robustness and practical deployability of LiDAR-based navigation across heterogeneous robots.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Joint Signal-Power and Direction of Arrival Estimation for Far-Field Targets Using Novel Metaheuristic Framework
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Accurate estimation of signal power and Direction of Arrival (DOA) from array data is a challenging problem with numerous applications in signal processing, radar, sonar and seismic exploration. Once the DOA information is gained, it is given to the beamformer network to place nulls in jammer directions, while maintaining the mainbeam in the desired look direction. Similarly, the estimated power is used to calculate the radar cross section that represent the effective reflecting area of the target. This work, proposes a unified framework based on the Artificial Protozoa Optimization (APO) Algorithm to jointly estimate the signal power and DOA of multiple far-field targets. A system model linking the estimated amplitudes to their corresponding power levels is formulated, and the joint estimation task is posed as a single dimensional search problem. A cost function based on Mean Square Error (MSE) is designed that defines the difference between actual and desired output of the system. This cost function neither require derivative information nor any strict statistical assumptions to explore the search space. It automatically pair the desired DOA with the relevant power corresponding to any particular target and does not require the multidimensional search. Simulation results verify that the proposed framework provides better estimation accuracy for both DOA and power of the far field targets even in the presence of low signal to noise ratio. The proposed framework is also compared with already existing algorithms in terms of estimation accuracy, MSE and robustness against noise.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Enhanced Corrosion Resistance and Aesthetic Properties of Titanium Alloys Through Stabilized Anodizing Processes: A Review
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This review provides an overview of developments in anodizing titanium and its alloys, focusing on enhancing aspects such as corrosion protection, surface morphology, and functional performance. As these parameters influence the growth mechanism, morphology, thickness, and crystallinity of anodic oxide films, this study focuses on how process parameters, including electrolyte composition (acid), temperature, applied voltage, and anodizing time, affect these properties. The study focuses on conventional anodizing in sulfuric acid electrolytes and on the use of novel, more environmentally friendly electrolytes, including deep eutectic solvents (DES). The review then highlights the application of green anodizing alternative, which enables precise tailoring of nanostructured TiO2 films, while significantly reducing environmental impact. The study also focused on how applied voltage and temperature affect the colors produced during anodizing, the corrosion rate, and the long-term performance of the protective layer in harsh environments. The review highlights stabilized anodizing’s key role in producing stable, color-variegated (different colors on the same surface), and corrosion-resistant coatings for aerospace, biomedical, and defense applications. Finally, the paper discusses future research directions to strengthen sustainable anodizing approaches and enhance understanding of how processing parameters govern surface performance.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: FlexICL: A Flexible Visual In-Context Learning Framework for Elbow and Wrist Ultrasound Segmentation
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Elbow and wrist fractures are the most common fractures in pediatric populations. Automatic segmentation of musculoskeletal structures in ultrasound (US) can improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning. Fractures appear as cortical defects but require expert interpretation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) can provide real-time feedback and highlight key structures, helping lightly trained users perform exams more confidently. However, pixel-wise human expert annotations required for AI model training remain time-consuming and costly. To address this challenge, we propose FlexICL, a novel and flexible in-context learning (ICL) framework designed for segmenting bony regions in US images. We applied it to a label-sparse setting, where only a very small subset of training frames contained human annotations, and the model segmented unseen test frames from different videos. We systematically investigated various image concatenation techniques and training strategies for visual ICL and introduced novel concatenation methods that significantly enhance model performance with limited labeled data. By integrating multiple context focus enhancement strategies, FlexICL achieves robust segmentation performance across four wrist and elbow US datasets while requiring only 5% of the training images. It outperforms state-of-the-art visual ICL models like Painter, MAE-VQGAN, and its backbone ViT-CNN by up to 52% Dice coefficient on 210 US sweeps. These initial results highlight the potential of FlexICL as an efficient and scalable solution for US image segmentation well-suited for medical imaging use cases where labeled data is scarce.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Frequency Recognition of Short-Time SSVEP Signal Using CORRCA-Based Spatio-Spectral Feature Fusion Framework
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Brain-computer interface (BCI) refers to the recognition of brain activity leading to generate corresponding commands to interact with external devices. Due to its safety and high time resolution, electroencephalogram (EEG) based BCIs have become popular. Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) is an EEG particularly attractive due to high signal to noise ratio (SNR) and robustness. A spatio-spectral feature fusion approach is introduced to recognize the frequency of short-time SSVEP using correlated component analysis (CORRCA). Two reference signals are generated by averaging each half of the training trials. The signal of each channel is passed through a filter bank designed to decompose into a predefined set of subbands. The spatial correlation coefficients are calculated between each subband of the test trial and the reference signals using CORRCA. The two sets of coefficients derived from two reference signals are merged and sorted in descending order. Thus obtained coefficients are weighted using a nonlinear function to define their contribution in frequency recognition. The weighted coefficients are fused to obtain a single coefficient for the target stimulus frequency of individual subband. The derived coefficients for each subband are weighted with another nonlinear function and fused to single coefficient for the target stimulus. A similar process is applied for each stimulus frequency and then the frequency corresponding to the highest coefficient is recognized as the target stimulus. The performance of the proposed method outperforms other existing algorithms to recognize the stimulus frequencies of SSVEP.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Trial Regeneration With Subband Signals for Motor Imagery Classification in BCI Paradigm
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures the electrical activities of human brain. It is an easy and cost effective tool to characterize motor imager (MI) task used in brain computer interface (BCI) implementation. The MI task is represented by short time trial of multichannel EEG. In this paper, the raw EEG trial is regenerated using narrowband signals obtained from individual channel. Each channel of EEG trial is decomposed into a set of subband signals using multivariate discrete wavelet transform. The selected subbands are organized in two different ways namely vertical arrangement of subbands (VaS) and horizontal arrangement of subbands (HaS) to regenerate the trials. The features are extracted from each of the arrangements using common spatial pattern (CSP). An optimum number of features are used to classify the motor imagery tasks represented by EEG trials. The effectiveness of two classifiers– linear discriminant analysis (LDA) and support vector machine (SVM) are studied. The performances of the proposed methods are evaluated using publicly available benchmark datasets. The experimental results show that it performs better than the recently developed algorithms.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Discriminative Feature Selection-Based Motor Imagery Classification Using EEG Signal
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Achieving a reliable classification of motor imagery (MI) tasks is a major challenge in brain–computer interface (BCI) implementation. The set of relevant and discriminative features plays an important role in the classification scheme. This paper presents a supervised approach to select discriminative features for the enhancement of MI classification using multichannel electroencephalography (EEG) signal. The dimension of multiband feature space is reduced using the feature selection method. Each trial of the multichannel EEG signal representing MI tasks is decomposed into a finite set of narrowband signals. The common spatial pattern-based features are extracted from each subband. The features obtained from the multiple subbands are combined to derive a high-dimensional feature vector. The neighborhood component analysis-based feature selection method is implemented to select the features that are relevant in performing an accurate classification. It is a nearest-neighbor-based approach to learn the feature weights with regularization by maximizing the average leave-one-out classification accuracy over the labeled training data. The selected features are used to train the support vector machine for classification. The features relatively irrelevant to the classification task are discarded, yielding a reduction of feature dimension. The evaluation of the proposed method is performed using BCI Competition III dataset 4a and IV dataset 2b. Both are publicly available datasets and are used as types of benchmark data to evaluate the MI classification algorithm to implement BCI. The obtained simulation results confirm the superiority of the proposed method compared to the recently developed algorithms.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Toward Higher Resolution Arctic Winter Sea Ice Concentration: Addressing Sentinel-1 Misclassification With AMSR2 Data Fusion
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Accurate and high-resolution sea ice concentration (SIC) products are needed for operational forecasting and climate monitoring. Passive microwave sensors, such as the advanced microwave scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2), provide daily SIC observations at 5-km resolution. However, this coarse spatial resolution constrains their capabilities. Whereas, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers high-resolution ice–water discrimination but is prone to classification errors in wind-roughened open water and land-fast ice. This study aims to obtain the strengths of both sensors to produce a robust km-scale SIC for winter Arctic conditions by applying an SAR–AMSR2 data fusion framework using a U-Net model trained on high-resolution pixel-level labels. The U-Net uses SAR features (HH, HV, and incidence angle) and AMSR2 inputs, with 13 feature combinations across two fusion strategies being evaluated: direct data-level fusion of AMSR2 brightness temperatures or preprocessed data-level fusion of AMSR2 SIC. The findings show that fusing AMSR2 SIC with SAR improves classification with mean intersection over union scores of 97.93% and 92.47% compared with SAR- and Landsat-derived validation data, with significant improvements in previously identified troublesome land-fast ice and open water regions. The preservation of spatial resolution in the fused SIC is also evaluated by using power spectral variance analysis, which confirms that the fusion does not degrade the effective spatial resolution of the final output. Overall, the approach presented in this study supports accurate, high-resolution winter SIC retrieval suitable for future operational forecasting and data assimilation, such as the Barents-2.5-km model, by preserving fine-scale features and reducing misclassification.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Adaptive Fusion of Aspect Constraint and Strain Model for InSAR 3-D Deformation Inversion
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Accurate and high-resolution monitoring of 3-D surface deformation is essential for analyzing and mitigating geological hazards. Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) has become a pivotal technique for monitoring surface deformation due to its unique advantages. However, the side-looking imaging geometry of near-polar orbiting satellites results in InSAR line-of-sight (LOS) measurements having severe insensitivity to the North–South (N-S) deformation component. Consequently, InSAR-LOS 3-D deformation inversion becomes an inherently ill-posed problem, severely restricting its application in the precise identification of geological hazards in mountainous areas. To address this challenge, this article proposes a novel InSAR-LOS 3-D deformation inversion method fusing terrain aspect constraints and strain models. This method integrates the aspect constraint and the strain model into a unified inversion framework, simultaneously leveraging the physical pointing of topography information and the spatial smoothness of the strain model to provide dual prior support for 3-D deformation inversion. Furthermore, specifically targeting terrain-sensitive regions with aspects near the N-S direction, the method introduces an adaptive window selection and dynamic regularization adjustment strategy, designed to mitigate local ill-posedness and enhance estimation accuracy. Simulation experiments confirm that the proposed method yields both a more accurate reconstruction and a higher fidelity surface deformation pattern than traditional approaches. Practical application in the Panzhou area, Guizhou, further verifies the robustness of the method: the proposed method successfully recovered a reasonable 3-D deformation field consistent with the topographic mechanism, with solution uncertainty significantly lower than that of comparative methods. This study confirms that the intelligent fusion of multisource physical priors is an effective approach to overcome the inherent geometric defects of InSAR-LOS observations, thereby directly achieving high-precision and physically credible 3-D deformation retrieval, making the method particularly effective for monitoring gravity-driven deformation in complex terrain.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Adaptive Rotation-Scaling Ensemble Patch Attack for Ship Detection in Remote Sensing Images
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Existing adversarial patch generation methods for remote sensing ship detection suffer from several limitations, including insufficient adaptability to patch size, inability to handle orientation variations of rotated ships, and poor transferability of adversarial patches. Considering these problems, this article first proposes an adaptive rotation-scaling ensemble patch attack method, named ARSEA, to enhance suitability of adversarial patches for ship sizes and orientations. Specifically, a adversarial patch is scaled according to the size of the rotated bounding box of the ship and rotated using the angle information combined with a location-aware mask, enabling precise alignment with ship targets of various sizes and orientations. For the last problem, a model ensemble attack strategy based on gradient direction consistency is proposed, where weights are adaptively assigned according to the cosine similarity between the gradients of multiple surrogate models. This guides the patch optimization toward the commonly vulnerable regions shared by multiple models, reduces gradient conflicts, and enhances the transferability of the patch. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the detection accuracy of ship targets. When integrating multiple detectors, the generated patch achieves approximately 60% mAP reduction and 50% target vanishing rate on three unknown black-box detection models. Furthermore, in multiclass attack scenarios, the proposed method also achieves an attack success rate of around 40%, showing strong transferability.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: HyTC-TaNet: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model Capturing Multiday Temporal Dependencies for Daily Mean Air Temperature Estimation With Spatial Applicability Analysis
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Air temperature is a fundamental indicator for climate monitoring, agricultural planning, and ecosystem management. Land surface temperature (LST) retrieved from thermal remote sensing is widely used as a critical proxy for air temperature. However, existing air temperature estimation studies predominantly rely on single-date LST and diurnal variations (e.g., the diurnal temperature cycle, DTC), overlooking the potential of multiday LST temporal dependencies and lacking explicit spatial representativeness assessments. To address these challenges, here we present a hybrid transformer-CNN daily mean air temperature (Ta) estimation network (HyTC-TaNet), which integrates Transformer-based temporal attention with convolutional feature extraction. While the area of applicability (AOA) metric is introduced to quantify spatial prediction confidence. Comparative experiments involving eight models, including HyTC-TaNet and seven benchmark algorithms, reveal that a 6–7 days temporal input window yields the best performance across all models. HyTC-TaNet achieves the highest accuracy, with RMSE = 1.429 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula>C, MAE = 1.101 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula>C, and <italic>R</italic><inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{2}$</tex-math></inline-formula> = 0.976, reducing errors by 0.273 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula>C (RMSE) and 0.219 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula>C (MAE) compared with concurrent day input. Spatial-temporal analysis further confirms that the optimal temporal sequence enriches historical and trend information, significantly enhancing estimation stability and spatial detail. Furthermore, the AOA of the model was assessed, confirming robust applicability in station-dense plains, while effectively flagging extrapolation risks over large water bodies and high-altitude ridges due to limited representativeness in the training data. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of coupling HyTC-TaNet with optimally selected multiday time series and spatial applicability assessment for precise, scalable air temperature estimation. The code will be made available on <uri>https://github.com/wanfengna/HyTC-TaNet</uri>.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: GBPSA: An Efficient Grid-Based Parallel Scoring Algorithm for Spatiotemporal Coverage Analysis of Large-Scale Remote Sensing Data
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Efficient selection of optimal spatiotemporal coverage from massive remote sensing datasets is a critical bottleneck in operational data centers, limiting real-time applications. Current systems rely on geometric overlay-based methods, which suffer from severe efficiency degradation (minutes to tens of minutes) for datasets exceeding tens of thousands of images and become computationally prohibitive under cloud coverage constraints. To address this, we propose a grid-based parallel scoring algorithm (GBPSA). The algorithm discretizes the spatial coverage of remote sensing images, user query areas, and cloud-covered regions into grids, and employs a combination of “grid code matching and dynamic scoring mechanism” to form a rapid screening method for spatiotemporal coverage, optimizing coverage effectiveness while mitigating cloud interference. Our approach leverages the inherent concurrency of spatial grids and establishes a flexible partitioning and deduplication merging strategy based on space-filling curves for the screening and processing of large-scale remote sensing data, significantly improving efficiency while ensuring the accuracy of the screening. Comprehensive evaluation using the GF-2 archive (over 70 000 images) demonstrates that GBPSA achieves an 89.2% reduction in processing time compared to prior state-of-the-art methods while maintaining equivalent coverage quality, with only a minimal (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$< $</tex-math></inline-formula>2%) increase in required image count. This significant performance advancement enables real-time applications including disaster response and precision agriculture, substantially enhancing the operational capabilities of modern remote sensing data centers.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A Deep Learning Model Combining CNN and Transformer for Rice Yield Estimation at County and Pixel Scales in Northeast China
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The increasing population and food demand require a timely and accurate large-scale rice yield estimation method to ensure food security and the development of global food trade. However, traditional methods suffer from insufficient spatio-temporal feature extraction and inability of county- and pixel-scale yield estimation in large-area yield prediction, limiting the accuracy of yield estimation. Taking Northeast China as our study area, we propose a deep learning model, zoned CNN-transformer (ZCT) combining a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a transformer module. We divided Northeast China into four environmentally similar regions through cluster analysis. In each region, the features in remote sensing data, meteorology, and soil properties were extracted and modeled. We compared the estimation accuracy of ZCT with that of CNN-transformer, zoned CNN-ALSTM, and zoned ANN-transformer. The results show that the ZCT model performs the best in the end-of-season model performance assessment, achieving an <italic>R</italic><sup>2</sup> of 0.89 and RMSE of 617.34 kg/ha at the county scale, and an <italic>R</italic><sup>2</sup> of 0.87 and RMSE of 678.04 kg/ha at the pixel scale. In addition, the ZCT model also performs well in the mid-season dynamics assessment, in which August is a critical period. We also suggest that normalized difference vegetation index, enhanced vegetation index, solar induced fluorescence, organic carbon content, and cation exchange capacity are the five most important feature variables in yield estimation through feature importance analysis. In conclusion, our ZCT model not only extracts features related to rice yield, but also reduces the impact of environmental differences on performance of the model in large regions through zonal modeling. This model realizes yield estimation at both county and pixel scales, providing an efficient and accurate solution for rice yield estimation in large regions and offering technical support for food security.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Semantic Segmentation of Flooded Vegetation in SAR Imagery: A Benchmark Dataset and Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Accurate flood extent mapping plays a critical role in disaster management and response. With the increasing availability of high-resolution and frequently acquired satellite imagery, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has become a valuable tool for flood delineation. However, one of the main challenges in SAR-based flood mapping remains the presence of vegetation, which obscures water surfaces and complicates detection. In this study, we introduce VegFlood, a reference dataset designed for training, validating, and testing deep learning models for semantic segmentation of flooded areas, including regions covered by vegetation. The dataset was constructed using publicly available Sentinel-1 SAR imagery, combined with high-resolution digital terrain models and hydrological observations from gauging stations. VegFlood comprises 1707 image–mask pairs from 39 gauging stations, geographically limited to the territory of Poland. To establish baseline performance on the VegFlood test set, we conducted a series of experiments using state-of-the-art deep learning models for flood segmentation. The experimental results consistently demonstrate that FV is the most difficult class to detect, achieving substantially lower Intersection over Union (IoU), User Accuracy (UA), and Producer Accuracy (PA) values compared to OW and NF classes. Among the evaluated models, RS-Mamba achieved the highest performance, reaching a mean IoU of 0.566, with UA of 0.689 and PA of 0.689.Further analysis shows that segmentation accuracy is strongly influenced by vegetation density, flood water level, and local geomorphological conditions. These results confirm the limitations of C-band SAR imagery for flooded vegetation detection and highlight the importance of dedicated datasets that explicitly account for FV as a separate semantic class.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Real-Time Hardware Acceleration of Recursive Orthogonal Subspace Projection for Automatic Hyperspectral Target Detection
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Orthogonal subspace projection (OSP) is a widely used concept to design hyperspectral imaging techniques for data exploitation. To make OSP-based techniques applicable to real-time processing, computing OSP must be also carried out in real-time. To realize its real-time capability, this article investigates field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for OSP in hardware implementation. Specifically, a new hardware accelerated architecture of recursive automatic target generation process (R-ATGP) is developed for unsupervised target detection. For a hyperspectral image cube with full <italic>L</italic> bands, R-ATGP can sustain an input rate of one pixel vector per <italic>L</italic> clock cycles and an output latency on the order of <italic>L</italic> clock cycles, making it the most efficient hardware accelerated architecture to date for automatic target generation process. Its hardware architecture is realized and validated by experiments via real hyperspectral image scenes performed on a cost-effective Xilinx Artix UltraScale+ FPGA which successfully demonstrates efficiency and efficacy of R-ATGP.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: MSRA-Net: Multiscale Residual Attention Network for Land Use Land Cover Scene Classification From Remote Sensing Images
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Remote sensing image classification plays an important role in environmental monitoring, urban planning, and disaster management. Current deep-learning methods have major limitations, including single-scale feature extraction, suboptimal attention mechanisms, high computational complexity, and poor spectral–spatial integration, indicating the need for stronger classification frameworks. In this article, we propose a novel multiscale residual attention network (MSRA-Net), a multiscale residual attention network, composed of several multicomponent approaches to address these limitations. MSRA-Net incorporates adaptive inverted bottleneck blocks for efficient multiscale feature extraction, which are followed by lightweight dense blocks to promote feature reuse and gradient flow. After that, a comprehensive attention mechanism is adopted for optimal spectral–spatial integration, incorporating multiscale channel attention to dynamically weigh feature importance. We use an advanced cross-scale feature fusion module with attention-weighted aggregation to effectively represent features across different scales, along with an atrous spatial pyramid pooling based classification head that captures contextual information using dilated convolutions. Training is performed using a comprehensive data augmentation framework, AdamW optimization, and an early stopping strategy to ensure robust classification performance. The proposed model is evaluated on two publicly diverse datasets, such as MLRSNet and NWPU-RESISC45. On these datasets, the proposed model achieved superior performance with overall class accuracies of 93.71% and 97.95%, respectively, significantly outperforming conventional pretrained and contemporary state-of-the-art models.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Sensing the Ionosphere Under Varying Electrodynamics During Extreme Cyclogenesis Using Real-Time/Near Real-Time Satellite Observations
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Severe meteorological conditions, such as tropical cyclones, may contribute in electrodynamical changes of the ionospheric layer in different ways. We search for possible physical mechanisms responsible in bringing such changes by considering an extremely severe cyclone “Biparjoy” as a case study using real-time/near real-time satellite observations. A significant growth in the atmospheric chemical potential (ACP) as spiral threads around the eyewall and right underneath the rainbands is observed during occurrence of numerous thunderstorms (K-index > 30), establishing a near-perfect correlation (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\rho \ = \ 0.99$</tex-math></inline-formula>). This observation confirms that the area under the cyclone became an ionized medium following the mutual interaction of the lightning activity and rain droplets. Moreover, the ionospheric total electron content (TEC) maps derived from the COSMIC-2 satellites reveal significant ionospheric enhancements (>10 TECU) in the form of concentric TEC shells, specifically, during cyclone’s peak intensity. This ionospheric intensification is driven by the mutual electric field variability from lightning activity added to the ACP growth from below that brought changes in the global electric circuit (GEC) through boundary layer conductivity. In addition, real-time global ionospheric maps and the novel ionospheric storm scale index maps exhibit significant performance in detecting meteorological influence onto the ionosphere, which is encouraging considering real-time ionospheric monitoring perspectives. While, ACP and TEC values exhibit a strong correlation (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\rho \ = \ 0.83$</tex-math></inline-formula>) providing evidence of cross-layer atmosphere coupling. Furthermore, NASA’s visible infrared imaging radiometer suite day/night band sensor nighttime radiance maps characterize the generation of atmospheric gravity waves (AGWs) that induced spasmodic S-type ripples in topside ionospheric density. However, the production of these ripples is instantaneous that was not observed during the rest of the analyzed period. These observations confirm that the sustained ionospheric enhancements are primarily attributed to the enhanced electrical conduction in GEC, rather than oscillatory AGW effects.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: VoroClust: Scalable Clustering for Remote Sensing
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Although supervised machine learning provides a powerful framework for image classification and segmentation, it requires comprehensive consistent datasets, which are not available for many remote-sensing applications. Remote-sensing datasets are expensive to collect, and each is acquired under different environmental conditions or with significant variations in system operating parameters. Unsupervised clustering algorithms analyze the structure of each dataset independently, rather than drawing on similarities with existing “training” examples, and are thus well suited for practical remote-sensing applications. We introduce VoroClust, a fast density-based unsupervised clustering algorithm applicable to high-resolution and high-dimensional data. VoroClust runs as fast as distance-based clustering methods, while capturing complex regional geometries at least as well as current-density-based methods. It uses a data-centered sphere cover to reduce computational demands, while still capturing data topology. It then propagates clusters outward from local peaks in density. We show that VoroClust provides fast state-of-the-art clustering for both high-resolution polarimetric synthetic aperture radar and high-dimensional hyperspectral imaging datasets.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Coarse-to-Fine Complementary Representation Network for Joint Hyperspectral and LiDAR Classification
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The fusion of hyperspectral image (HSI) data and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data has long been a research hot spot in remote sensing. Nevertheless, most of the existing fusion methods directly take HSI and LiDAR data as model inputs, without adequately addressing the spectral redundancy caused by the high-dimensional correlations inherent in the HSI, or the cross-modal spatial redundancy induced by structural overlap in complex HSI and LiDAR datasets. In addition, although spectral, spatial, and other attribute features have been extensively explored, the latent and complex relationships among features remain insufficiently modeled. To overcome these, this article proposes a coarse-to-fine collaborative representation network (CFCRNet). In the coarse-grained feature learning stage, a spatial reconstruction module models the discriminability score of spatial positions within a single channel and derives a spatial attention weight formula based on this score, which can be reused across all channels for spatial information reconstruction. A spectral redundancy removal module integrates spectral grouping and spectral normalization to reduce global spectral band correlations, and focuses on suppressing redundant components in local spectral variations, thereby facilitating efficient subsequent feature fusion. In the fine-grained feature learning stage, a multihead factorized attention fusion module focuses on selecting and fusing common and distinctive features, and explicitly models feature dependencies to enhance the discriminability of fused representations. Based on an integrated “redundancy removal–feature learning” mechanism, the proposed model can capture more effective complementary features under complex land-cover backgrounds. Experimental evaluations on three publicly available datasets show that the CFCRNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in land-cover classification tasks.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Reflectance Consistency Between MERSI-II and MODIS in Northeast China Under Varying Conditions
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The FY-3D satellite, launched by the China Meteorological Administration, carries the second-generation medium resolution spectral imager (MERSI-II). With the channel configuration similar to that of the moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer (MODIS), MERSI-II is one of the important data sources for global medium-resolution multispectral observations. For better usage of MERSI-II data, this study analyzed the differences in top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance and land surface reflectance (LSR) observed by these two sensors under different conditions of solar zenith angle (SZA), land cover types, and aerosol optical depth (AOD) through a cross-comparison of synchronous images. The results show that MERSI-II and MODIS TOA reflectance exhibit strong correlations across visible bands (<italic>R</italic> > 0.7, <italic>p</italic><0.01), although MERSI-II systematically overestimates TOA reflectance at high SZA. For LSR, consistency in visible bands is maintained under low AOD conditions (0–0.4), but the discrepancy increases sharply with increasing AOD and the degree of difference differs across spectral bands. In addition, the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) shows the highest consistency between the two sensors over croplands and the lowest over forested areas. When AOD > 0.4, MERSI-II LSR-based NDVI becomes lower than that of MODIS, especially in densely vegetated regions. The findings provide an important reference for the product upgrade of MERSI-II data and the collaborative inversion of vegetation parameters using multisource remote sensing data in the future.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: GPU-Accelerated High-Resolution Geostationary-Satellite-Based Atmospheric Motion Vector Retrieval
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Satellite-derived atmospheric motion vectors (AMVs) provide essential wind field data crucial for numerical weather prediction (NWP) and nowcasting applications. However, current operational AMV products typically offer relatively low spatial resolution, limiting their effectiveness in meeting precise meteorological forecasting requirements. Retrieving AMVs at higher spatial resolutions significantly increases computational demand, hindering their application in real-time operational scenarios. To address this challenge, this article introduces a novel GPU-accelerated (graphics processing unit) algorithm, based on OpenACC (ACCelerators), designed specifically to improve computational efficiency in the target-tracking part of the AMV retrieval algorithm. The proposed method decomposes complex calculations into parallel tasks suitable for efficient processing by GPUs. Additionally, to address the limited memory capacity of individual GPUs, a block-based computational strategy is developed, allowing for efficient use of multiple GPUs to process larger datasets. A comparative analysis at 48, 12, and 6 km resolutions showed that, at 6 km, OpenMP on a 48-core CPU achieved a 40 × speedup, while single- and dual-GPU configurations reached approximately 50 × and 110 ×, respectively. The hybrid OpenACC+OpenMP strategy, combining one GPU with 48 CPU cores, delivered the highest acceleration at around 140 ×, with all GPU-based methods maintaining near-lossless accuracy relative to the CPU baseline. This article provides a practical and effective solution for real-time high-resolution AMV retrieval, significantly improving the timeliness of critical meteorological services such as typhoon monitoring and data assimilation in NWP systems.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: XCC-YOLO: An Enhanced YOLOv11 Architecture for Mining Detection in Satellite Imagery
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The precise detection of mining activities using deep learning (DL) on satellite imagery has been paving innovative paths for environmental monitoring and preservation, regulatory compliance, and natural resource management in the mining industry. Nevertheless, existing DL based models confront some constraints: 1) Critical implementation aspects are not specified, which limits reproducibility. 2) Most were evaluated on a single train-validation split, which may not fully reflect model generalization. 3) Benchmarking was done only against the baseline model and are implemented on slightly outdated baseline DL models, with the highest AP@50 reaching just 0.575 on a publicly available mining detection dataset. To address these limitations, this study proposes an enhanced DL model, based on the YOLOv11 architecture, for surface mining detection. The proposed architecture incorporates four channel attention modules to strengthen feature representation, three content-aware reassembly of features (CARAFE) upsampling modules to replace the standard upsampling operations to enable content-aware feature upscaling, and an extra detection head to enhance multiscale detection. The model is assessed on a new Canada-wide mining detection dataset. Compared to baseline YOLOv11, the proposed model demonstrates a 0.9% increment in AP@50, while outperforming MFTA-YOLO, which is previously identified as the best performing model for mining detection domain, by 2.9% in AP@50. Furthermore, it has consistent improvements across multiple different splits, indicating reliable generalization capability. Visual review of predicted outputs confirms more accurate detection, while Grad-CAM visualizations further validate that the proposed model outperforms the existing state-of-the-art models.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: StyleDe-CD: Dual-Level Style Disentanglement for Semisupervised Change Detection
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Semisupervised change detection (SSCD) is a promising approach for reducing the annotation burden in bitemporal remote sensing imagery. However, learning robust representations remains challenging due to style variations across and within temporal images, which often dominate visual differences and interfere with semantic change modeling. These challenges can be attributed to two levels of style-semantic entanglement: 1) cross-temporal style discrepancies caused by acquisition variations (e.g., illumination shifts and seasonal changes), which may confuse the model and increase sensitivity to superficial appearance differences; and 2) intratemporal style heterogeneity introduced by diverse background characteristics (e.g., land-cover diversity and vegetation density differences), which can bias feature learning and obscure meaningful semantic changes. To address these challenges, we propose StyleDe-CD, a dual-level style disentanglement framework for SSCD. At the input level, we design a stochastic spectralphotometric style augmentation (SSPSA) strategy, which combines spectral style alignment and photometric transformations to mitigate cross-temporal discrepancies and enhance robustness to appearance variations. At the feature level, we introduce an intratemporal style mixing (ISM) mechanism that randomly mixes feature statistics across samples within a minibatch, encouraging the model to suppress background-specific styles and focus on semantic changes. Extensive experiments on the LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and CDD benchmarks demonstrate that StyleDe-CD consistently achieves strong and competitive performance compared to existing semisupervised baselines, particularly under lowlabel regimes, indicating its effectiveness in SSCD.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Multisource Data Integration Study on the Spatiotemporal Characteristics and Driving Mechanisms of Ground Displacement: Huainan City, China, Case Study
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Huainan City is a major energy base in China, characterized by complex geological conditions and frequent ground deformation driven by multiple factors. Previous studies have often focused on single causes, making it difficult to fully reveal the combined drivers of ground deformation. There is, therefore, an urgent need to integrate multisource, multimodal data for comprehensive analysis. In this study, Small Baseline Subset Interferometry Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) processing of 150 Sentinel-1A scenes was used to obtain ground deformation information in Huainan from January 2019 to December 2023. These deformation data were combined with Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Follow-On (GRACE-FO) groundwater measurements, population density, road density, and gross domestic product to perform factor detection and interaction factor detection using the optimal parameter-based geographical detector (OPGD) method, quantitatively assessing the relationships between deformation and multiple influencing factors. The results show significant regional variability in deformation rates across Huainan, with maximum deformation and uplift rates of 127 mm/year and 63 mm/year occurring in active and closed mines, respectively. Groundwater change plays a key role in ground deformation, exhibiting a hydrology-dominated, multifactor coupling pattern. Cross-validation with leveling and well measurements confirms the high reliability of both the InSAR-derived deformation and GRACE-FO inverted groundwater storage changes; the trends in groundwater storage and ground deformation both display periodic fluctuations. Finally, detailed analyses of three characteristic zones, namely the urban district, the mining area, and a ground-mounted photovoltaic power plant. This study developed a comprehensive analysis framework for ground deformation based on multisource, multimodal data fusion and the OPGD method, and systematically quantified the coupled relationships between deformation and multiple driving factors in Huainan. The framework demonstrates good scalability and can provide scientific support for long-term monitoring and risk management in resource-based cities with similar geological conditions.
